picks.title: Putting sign language AI into users' hands
picks.excerpt: DeepMind shipped SL2T, a massively multilingual sign-language-to-text translation model trained on 100,000+ hours across 50+ sign languages, into Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11. It is the first consumer deployment of sign-language translation research.
picks.rationale: Research that actually left the lab: 50+ sign languages inside a shipping keyboard makes sign language an input modality product teams can design for today, not a paper.

picks.title: Empty shelves or lost keys? Recall is the bottleneck for parametric factuality
picks.excerpt: Google Research's 'knowledge profiling' framework shows frontier LLMs encode 95-98% of tested facts yet still fail to recall 26-34% of them. The failure mode is retrieval, not missing knowledge - a direct reframing of why models hallucinate.
picks.rationale: Reframes hallucination as a retrieval failure inside a model that already knows the answer, which changes whether you reach for better prompting and cueing or for more training data.

picks.title: Teaching AI the biology of antibodies speeds drug discovery
picks.excerpt: Boston University researchers built an antibody-specific language model that concentrates on the six binding loops instead of the whole protein, improving binding-strength prediction by up to 27%. Encoding domain biology into the architecture beat treating antibodies as generic proteins.
picks.rationale: A 27% gain that came from building domain structure into the architecture rather than scaling it - the clearest recent argument that specialist models still beat generic ones on specialist data.

picks.title: New AI technique helps robots complete tasks twice as fast by letting them 'think ahead'
picks.excerpt: Researchers built VLASH, a system that lets a robot plan its next action while still executing the current one, cutting reaction delay up to 11.8x and roughly doubling task completion speed. The gain comes with no extra compute overhead.
picks.rationale: An 11.8x latency cut with no extra compute comes purely from overlapping planning and execution - a scheduling idea that transfers to any agent stuck waiting on its own next step.

picks.title: Human biological datacenter to launch to train world model of human biology
picks.excerpt: Vivodyne is opening what it calls the world's largest human biological datacenter: 12 robotic labs running 3.1 million lab-grown human tissue trials a year. The output is training data for an AI world model spanning 22 organ systems.
picks.rationale: Robotic labs built to manufacture training data rather than run one-off experiments - the missing-dataset problem being answered with industrial-scale wet-lab throughput.
